_comment: Declarative description of the validated, turnkey demos the Web UI can run end-to-end. Each entry is the data behind examples/rtdetr-aerial-sheep/run.sh (aerial-sheep) and examples/rtdetr-pcb/run.sh (pcb). pipeline.py reads these fields; it never hard-codes a demo. Paths are relative to the working root (ROOT, normally /work). Only models whose model_id matches `model_id` here have a deploy recipe; anything else is flagged needs_recipe.

aerial-sheep.label: RT-DETR + Aerial Sheep
aerial-sheep.dataset_label: Aerial Sheep (1 class, dense tiny objects)
aerial-sheep.blurb: COCO already has a 'sheep' class, so the stock model gives a real non-zero baseline; the aerial/tiny-object domain shift leaves large fine-tuning headroom. Validated: deployed mAP@50 0.19 -> 0.95.

report_meta.model_desc: RT-DETR R50vd. Baseline = stock COCO-80 model (has a 'sheep' class); fine-tuned = 30 epochs on aerial-sheep (1 class).
report_meta.dataset_desc: Aerial/drone sheep detection, 1 class; dense small objects. eval on 200 valid images.

pcb.label: RT-DETR + PCB Defects
pcb.blurb: No PCB-defect class exists in COCO-80, so the stock model scores an honest mAP 0; fine-tuning on 6 defect classes is what raises it. Both eval legs are built against the 6-class TARGET labels.

report_meta.model_desc: RT-DETR R50vd. Baseline = stock COCO-80 model (no PCB-defect class -> honest mAP 0); fine-tuned = 30 epochs on PKU/HRIPCB (6 defect classes).
report_meta.dataset_desc: PCB surface-defect detection, 6 classes (mouse_bite, spur, missing_hole, short, open_circuit, spurious_copper); 6370 train. Eval on 200 test images.
